newsitem.title: INDIA: India regrets U.S. trade move.
newsitem.headline: India regrets U.S. trade move.

text.p: India said on Thursday that it regretted a U.S. decision to keep it on a "watch list" of countries potentially subject to unilateral trade sanctions.

The Foreign Ministry said in a statement the U.S. decision to keep India on its "Special 301" list was not "in consonance with the positive trend in the development of commercial and business relations between India and the United States".

The U.S. Trade Representative on Wednesday released its Special 301 annual review of other countries' safeguards protecting intellectual property rights. A nation judged to have a persistently poor record could be subject to U.S. trade sanctions.
"The Government of India notes with regret the decision of the U.S. Government to continue to place India on the priority watch list under their 'Special 301' provisions," the statement said.
The ministry said both countries are members of the World Trade Organisation, which it said provides the appropriate forum for discussing and resolving such matters.

Growing bilateral cooperation in trade and economic matters in recent years demonstrated that U.S. companies "have a keen appreciation of the rights and safeguards provided under the administrative, legal and judicial processes in India", it said.
